subject: physics
title: Energy stored by a capacitor
key_idea: The energy stored by a capacitor is the area under its p.d.–charge graph. This gives W = ½QV = ½CV² = ½Q²/C. Capacitors can release their energy very quickly.

blocks.text: Charging a capacitor means pushing charge onto the plates against the p.d. already there. The energy stored is the work done in doing this.

items: The p.d. is V = Q/C, so a graph of p.d. against charge is a straight line through the origin.
Moving a small charge ΔQ at p.d. V needs work V ΔQ. That is the area of a thin strip under the graph.
Adding all the strips, the total energy stored is the area under the graph.
The area is a triangle: ½ × base × height.

diagram.alt: A straight line graph of potential difference against charge for a capacitor, through the origin. The area under the line is the energy stored.

bands.label: Area under the line = energy stored

blocks.label: Energy stored by a capacitor
where: V = final p.d. across the capacitor (V)

items: Energy stored is the area under the p.d.–charge graph.
The area is a triangle, so W = ½QV.
It is half of QV because the p.d. builds up from zero as the charge builds up.

blocks.text: Substituting C = Q/V into W = ½QV gives two more forms. Use whichever fits the quantities you know.

items.text: Replace Q to get W = ½CV².
Replace V to get W = ½Q²/C.

items: For the same capacitor, doubling the p.d. makes the energy four times larger, because W ∝ V².
For the same charge, a larger capacitance stores less energy, because W ∝ 1/C.

items: Energy depends on the square of the p.d. or of the charge.

checks.q: A 2200 μF capacitor is charged to 9.0 V. Calculate the energy stored.
Explain why the energy stored by a capacitor is ½QV and not QV.
checks.a: The p.d. rises from zero to V as the charge builds up, in proportion to the charge. The energy is the area of the triangle under the p.d.–charge graph, which is ½QV.

checks.q: The p.d. across a capacitor is doubled. State and explain the effect on the energy stored.
checks.a: The energy becomes four times larger. W = ½CV², so W is proportional to V² when C is constant.

blocks.text: Uses of capacitors as energy stores

items: A camera flash: the capacitor charges slowly from a battery, then releases its energy in a very short burst.
A defibrillator: a capacitor stores energy and delivers it quickly to the patient in one pulse.
A backup supply: a capacitor keeps the memory of a device powered for a short time if the main supply is cut off.
A capacitor can release energy much faster than a battery, but it stores much less energy for its size.
Capacitors suit uses that need energy delivered quickly.
They store less energy than a battery of the same size.
